---
title: "Noninteractive builds"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

CI jobs, scripts and workspace launchers that run a report build in the
background need three things from quartifyr: a way to find out what is wrong
before a long build starts, a bound on how long the build can take, and an
unambiguous outcome when it finishes. A render that left placeholders unfilled
must not look like a success.

## Check the project first

`check_report_project()` never renders. It reads the project's files and
returns a data frame of findings, so a launcher can show problems before
queueing a job:

```{r}
findings <- quartifyr::check_report_project("report.qmd")
findings
#> ── 1 error, 0 warnings
#> ✖ [missing-sidecar] {rpfy}:conc-time.png (line 191) has no metadata sidecar at ...

if (any(findings$severity == "error")) stop("fix the errors above before rendering")
```

Each row has a `check` identifier, a `severity` (`"error"` or `"warning"`), the
`path` concerned and a `message`. It covers:

* the preconditions `render_report()` itself enforces (the shell `.qmd`, the
  `output-dir: report/shell` setting, the reportifyr `*_init.json` marker, the
  reference-doc and `standard_footnotes.yaml`);
* the required Quarto extensions, by scanning `_extensions/` rather than asking
  the Quarto CLI;
* every `{rpfy}:` placeholder in the `.qmd`, plus `synopsis:` `image:` entries:
  the artifact exists under `OUTPUTS/figures` or `OUTPUTS/tables`, its
  `<stem>_<ext>_metadata.json` sidecar exists and parses, and the abbreviations
  and `meta_type` it references are defined in `standard_footnotes.yaml`;
* placeholders that are the last thing in their section, which crashes
  reportifyr's `build_report()`.

Placeholders inside HTML comments or fenced code blocks are ignored, and files
pulled in with `{{< include >}}` are not scanned.

`render_report()` shares the precondition checks with this function, so the two
cannot disagree. It does not stop on missing artifacts: those are reported in
its result instead (below).

## Bound the render

`render_report()` runs `quarto render` with a timeout and kills the whole process
tree (Deno, Pandoc, knitr) when it expires or the R session is interrupted:

```{r}
quartifyr::render_report("report.qmd", quarto_timeout = 300)
```

The default is 600 seconds and `Inf` disables the limit. A timeout signals an
error of class `quartifyr_quarto_timeout` whose message includes the tail of
Quarto's stderr. To use an app-local Quarto instead of the one on `PATH`, pass
`quarto_bin = "/path/to/quarto"` or set `QUARTO_PATH`.

## Read the outcome

`render_report()` returns the three docx paths it always did (`shell`, `draft`,
`final`) plus:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `"ok"`, `"warning"` or `"error"` |
| `artifacts` | `role`, `path`, `sha256` and `bytes` for each file produced |
| `unfilled_placeholders` | `{rpfy}:` strings still unresolved in the draft or final docx |
| `missing_metadata` | artifacts the shell references that have no metadata sidecar |
| `warnings`, `errors` | the messages behind a non-`"ok"` status |
| `log_dir` | reportifyr's log directory for the project |

`status` describes whether the delivered document is complete. `"error"` means
placeholders were left unfilled, or a LibreOffice step you asked for
(`recalculate_fields`, `resolve_same_page_crossrefs`) failed. `"warning"` means
the document is complete but reportifyr flagged something.

Pass `strict = TRUE` to turn any non-`"ok"` status into an error of class
`quartifyr_render_incomplete`. The condition carries the full result as
`$result`:

```{r}
result <- tryCatch(
  quartifyr::render_report("report.qmd", strict = TRUE),
  quartifyr_render_incomplete = function(e) {
    print(e$result$unfilled_placeholders)
    stop(e)
  }
)
```

The default is `strict = FALSE`, so existing callers keep receiving a value.

With reportifyr's default settings, a missing metadata sidecar makes
`build_report()` itself fail rather than leaving a placeholder behind. In that
case `render_report()` signals an error of class `quartifyr_pass2_failed` that
names the missing sidecars.

## The script

`inst/scripts/render.R` wraps the same call for a shell or a launcher. Run it
with the project as the working directory, so the project's renv library is the
one that activates:

```bash
cd path/to/project
Rscript "$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts", "render.R", package = "quartifyr"))')" \
  --project . --shell report.qmd --status draft --json --strict
```

The JSON result goes to stdout and nothing else does; progress and errors go to
stderr. The exit status is 0 only when the render finished (and, with
`--strict`, its status is `"ok"`). Any error, including a Quarto failure or
timeout, prints a JSON object with `status: "error"`, an `errors` array and an
`error_class`, and exits 1. Bad usage exits 2. Run it with `--help` for the
remaining options (`--quarto-timeout`, `--quarto-bin`, `--reference-doc`,
`--recalculate-fields`, ...).

A successful result looks like this:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "shell": "/work/project/report/shell/report.docx",
  "draft": "/work/project/report/draft/report-draft.docx",
  "final": null,
  "artifacts": [
    {"role": "shell", "path": "/work/project/report/shell/report.docx", "sha256": "9c8a...", "bytes": 44379},
    {"role": "draft", "path": "/work/project/report/draft/report-draft.docx", "sha256": "fa9e...", "bytes": 341570}
  ],
  "warnings": [],
  "errors": [],
  "unfilled_placeholders": [],
  "missing_metadata": [],
  "log_dir": "/work/project/.rpfy-logs"
}
```

The shape is documented as a JSON Schema in
`system.file("schemas", "render-result.schema.json", package = "quartifyr")`.

## In GitHub Actions

The composite action takes a `strict` input (default `'false'`) and exposes the
result's status as a `status` output:

```yaml
- uses: jprybylski/quartifyr@v1
  id: render
  with:
    shell-qmd: report.qmd
    strict: 'true'
```
